The CapEx differentials for all new building and facilities costs in ASEAN and India are at least 10% greater than China and, owing to much higher EPC expenses, perhaps up to 10 times greater in the United States and Europe (although recent data are limited owing to the rarity of projects in the United States and Europe since 2014). Higher startup costs outside China are also expected because of longer design and permitting timelines and higher construction soft costs. The results of Figure 26 also depend on assumed facility size. The NLR polysilicon cost models were set to represent the approximate average of the top 10 largest producers in China (200,000 t/yr), the largest ASEAN producer (OCI Malaysia, 35,000 t/yr), the largest U.S. producer (Hemlock, 35,000 t/yr), and the largest European producer (Wacker Bavaria, Germany, 60,000 t/yr) in 2024. India was not analyzed because its production is much more significant downstream—beginning with wafers—and in 2024 it had no known production of polysilicon. The downstream cost model results reflect the more likely scenario in 2024 that PV manufacturers in India were importing polysilicon to make wafers or would have imported polysilicon within the imported cells for module assembly (Jacobo 2024d). 38 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2.6.5 Upstream Inputs for Polysilicon This section provides limited information on priority inputs to the polysilicon production process. Many other upstream inputs are not discussed here due to limited supply chain information or relatively low importance. • mg-Si: See Section 2.7. • Graphite/carbon heating elements: Graphite heating elements and specialty gaskets are sourced from a mixture of foreign and domestic suppliers. • Hydrogen and hydrochloric acid: These common feedstock chemicals serve many research and industrial activities. The United States has a strong supply base for these chemicals, and local supply can be used. For example, the Dow Chemical plant in Midland, Michigan, is 13 miles from the Hemlock polysilicon facility. Another Dow Chemical plant in Knoxville, Tennessee, is 73 miles from the Wacker polysilicon facility. • Equipment: The supply chain for U.S. polysilicon equipment is local, because every manufacturer has its own unique approach and patents. This specialization is another reason for the higher U.S. CapEx. The priority inputs for polysilicon production and their relative costs are given in Table 4 in $/kg.
